title: Chicken Tagine
subtitle: Slow-braised chicken with chickpeas and green olives
excerpt: Boneless chicken thighs braised with chickpeas, green olives and saffron in a warm spice broth built on cumin, coriander, cinnamon and ginger. The sauce reduces to a thick, perfumed stew that is best served over couscous or with flatbread. The saffron is not optional here; it provides a floral depth the dish depends on.
sourceNotes: Tagine is named after the conical clay pot used for slow-cooking in North Africa; Moroccan chicken tagines draw on a spice vocabulary that blends Arab, Berber and Andalusian influences developed over many centuries.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: This improves markedly if made the day before and reheated. The spices deepen overnight.

content.text: Dissolve the saffron in two tablespoons of warm water before it goes into the pot and give it a few minutes to steep. This releases the colour and flavour more fully than adding the threads directly. The olives go in near the end of cooking so they stay plump rather than turning soft and bitter. Preserved lemons are a traditional addition if you have them; add two quarters with the olives and skip the fresh lemon juice.
Heat the olive oil in a wide, heavy-based pot over a high heat. Season the chicken thighs and brown in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden. Remove to a plate.

Reduce the heat to medium. Add the onion to the same pot and cook for 6 to 8 minutes until softened. Add the garlic, fresh ginger, cumin, ground coriander, cinnamon and sweet paprika. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring, until the spices are fragrant.
Add the tinned tomatoes, chickpeas and saffron water. Stir, then return the chicken to the pot, pushing the pieces into the sauce. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook for 30 minutes.
Remove the lid and add the green olives and lemon juice. Simmer uncovered for 15 to 20 minutes until the sauce has thickened and the chicken is very tender. Taste and adjust salt.
Scatter generously with fresh coriander and serve over couscous, with flatbread for mopping the sauce.

items.cause: Lid was on throughout and the liquid could not reduce
items.fix: Remove the lid for the final 20 minutes of cooking and simmer on a medium heat until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

items.cause: Spices were not cooked out properly or chicken was not browned
items.fix: Add another pinch of cinnamon and cumin, stir and cook for 5 more minutes. A little more lemon juice at the end will also brighten the dish.
